resources.string: Enables GlyphWorks to detect presses of the Essential Key so you can control Glyph Toys: press once for a Glyph Touch action, twice to switch to the next toy, three times to return to the background toy. The service observes hardware key presses and consumes the ones it recognises, so Essential Space does not open on top of the toy; it also watches Essential Space window events to dismiss it when the system still reacts to a captured press. It never reads screen content, and nothing it observes is stored or transmitted.
Glyph Toys, cycled with the Essential Key

GlyphWorks uses an accessibility service to detect presses of your phone’s Essential Key, including on the lock screen and Always-On Display. This is the only way a normal app can react to that key.

What the service does:
• Listens for Essential Key presses and consumes them so Essential Space does not open
• Single press: Glyph Touch action on the current toy
• Double press: switch to the next toy
• Triple press: return to the background toy

What the service does NOT do:
• It cannot and does not read your screen content
• It does not store or transmit anything it observes — key presses are counted in memory and turned into a toy action

On the next screen, enable “GlyphWorks” under Downloaded apps.

GlyphWorks listens for your phone’s Essential Key through an accessibility service — the only way a regular app can react to that key, even on the lock screen and Always-On Display.

With the listener on:
• Press once — Glyph Touch action on the current toy
• Press twice — switch to the next toy
• Press three times — return to the background toy

The service never reads your screen content and never collects or transmits any data. You can skip this step; the key simply keeps its stock behaviour.
Listener running — the Essential Key is yours
Listener off — enable it now or skip for later

Nothing OS shows one Glyph Toy at a time. Select “GlyphWorks” as your always-on toy and every screen in this app — clock, compass, dice, visualizer and friends — takes over the matrix, Always-On Display included.
Pick “GlyphWorks” in the list that opens, then come back here.
Each permission powers exactly one thing, and all of them are optional — skip any and the related toy just sits things out.
The Timer chimes when it runs out, and you’ll hear about new GlyphWorks releases.
The Music Visualizer dances to what’s playing. Audio is analysed on-device, never stored, never sent anywhere.
Corrects the Compass for magnetic declination and anchors the Solar Path to your sky.
Guarantees the Timer chime lands on the second, even when the phone is dozing.
The listener is on — now pick your pressing style. You can change this any time from the main screen.
Press once for the toy’s action, twice to jump to the next toy, three times to return to the background toy. Fast, and kind to muscle memory.

Double-press opens a blinking toy selector on the matrix; single presses then cycle through the toys, and the highlighted one is chosen after a short pause. Outside the menu, a single press still fires the toy’s action.

The app arrives with a set of toys ready to run — clock, compass, dice, music visualizer and a dozen more — and the Toys tab is where you pick between them and reorder the cycle.

The Create tab is the other half: your own designs, drawn cell by cell, still or animated, and played on the matrix like any other toy. You can share them as files, too.

Anything in this app that is not obvious has a short guide in the Tutorials tab — including a demo of the editor that acts out every gesture on the real thing, rather than describing it.
Or carry on — Create is one tap away in the navigation bar whenever you want it.

Your Glyph Matrix is officially over-qualified. Everything you just set up — and plenty you haven’t seen yet — lives in the main screen: reorder toys, tweak their settings, or revisit any of these steps.\n\nNow go press that key.

GlyphWorks only works on Nothing phones with a Glyph Matrix — Phone (3) or Phone (4a) Pro running Nothing OS.\n\nThis device has neither the matrix nor the Essential Key the app is built around, so there is nothing for it to do here.
When on, all Essential Key presses control Glyph Toys. When off, the key behaves normally.
Double-press opens a blinking on-glyph selector; single-press cycles toys, and the shown toy is set automatically after a few seconds. Single-press still triggers toy actions outside the menu.
Automatic brightness on — the Glyph follows the room light. Tap to turn off.
Automatic brightness off. Tap to let the Glyph follow the room light.
Drag the handle to change the cycle order
Short guides for the parts of this app that are least obvious — tap a topic.

A guided demo of the editor, with every gesture acted out
Every design starts with the + beside the navigation bar. It is there on the Create tab and nowhere else.

A name is suggested for you and the drawing starts on the phone you are holding — each Glyph Matrix size is a separate drawing, and the other one can be added later. This is the answer you cannot change afterwards: static is a single still picture, dynamic adds a timeline of frames. The demo picks dynamic.

The black disc is the Glyph Matrix, drawn where it sits on the back of the phone. Pick one of the three shades under it — “off” is the eraser — then drag across the disc to paint every cell your finger crosses; pinch with two fingers to zoom in. Undo takes back a whole stroke rather than one pixel, and beside it sit redo, clear and fill.

The strip is your frames. Duplicate copies the one you are on — copy, nudge a few pixels, repeat is how an animation gets drawn — and + adds a blank one after it. Nothing says so, so it is worth remembering: a frame is moved by pressing and holding it until it lifts, then dragging it along the strip. Each frame has its own length, set by the − and + on the left.

The disc in the corner is your animation actually running, at the lengths you just set — the canvas behind it only ever shows the one frame you are drawing. Tap it and it grows to nearly the whole screen; tap again to send it back.

Four buttons, left to right. Play runs the animation on the real Glyph Matrix, and pause puts the frame you are editing back on it — pressing play, or changing anything at all, also makes this the design the matrix keeps afterwards. The eye hides the preview disc when it sits over what you are drawing. Sparkles opens the design assistant: describe what you want, or hand it a photo, and it draws or animates it for you. The sliders are Design settings, which we are opening now — repeat, the Essential Key and artwork for the other phone size live behind them, the three easiest things in the editor to miss.

Play once rests on the first frame and plays the design through on a press of the Essential Key; play / pause runs it and lets a press stop and start it. Only play / pause has a repeat setting — which is why it just came and went.
This is repeat: on, the animation loops until you pause it; off, it plays through once and holds on the last frame. The whole shaded row is the switch — icon or sentence, either works.
Each Glyph Matrix size is a separate drawing, and this adds a blank canvas for the other one. Nothing is ever scaled between them.
That is the whole editor. Nothing in this demo was saved or sent to the matrix — the Create tab is where the real one starts.
Stop the system from acting on the key so this app gets it
Do NOT disable the Essential Space or Essential Recorder apps — just tell the system to wait before acting on the key:
In Settings → Intelligence Toolkit → Essential Key Settings, enable “Activate with single tap before use”.
In Settings → Intelligence Toolkit → Essential Voice, disable “Activate via Essential Key”.
This stops the system from reacting to the key directly. If a pop-up still slips through on some firmware, GlyphWorks dismisses it automatically.
Fires the current toy’s action: roll the dice, flip the coin, +1 the counter, start or pause the timer. Toys without an action simply ignore it.
Switches to the next enabled toy in your configured order, wrapping around at the end of the list.
Jumps straight back to the first toy in your list — the Ambient background — from anywhere.
The current toy starts blinking on the matrix: you are now choosing a toy, not switching yet.
Each press shows the next toy, still blinking. Keep pressing to browse the whole list. (Outside the selector, a single press still fires the toy’s action.)
Commits the blinking toy: it stops blinking and becomes the current toy.
Five seconds without a press and the blinking toy is set automatically. Every press restarts the countdown.
Leaves the selector and returns to the Ambient background, exactly like in regular mode.
